title: DC circuits lane 2: dividers, timing and stored energy
mission: Curate the listed uncovered DC subtopics only: dividers, timing constants and field-energy storage, each with explicit component and operating conditions. Check the supplied inventory first; any overlap with lane-1 records becomes a deferred overlap note, never a renamed clone. Successive batches; no circuit chain required.
priorities: Resistive voltage divider output under stated loading conditions
RC time constant from resistance and capacitance
boundaries: Already covered in b01-b04, do not resubmit: ohmic voltage-current relation, signed terminal power, two-resistor series and parallel equivalents, uniform-conductor resistance, conductivity-resistivity reciprocity, linear resistance temperature dependence, average current from charge, DC conductance, area-mean current density, single-carrier drift current, DC source terminal characteristic, carrier density from material content, copper temperature-coefficient calibration.
Ohmic behavior is an applicability condition, not a universal device law; separate signed quantities from nonnegative magnitudes.
RC charging and discharging curves need exp and must be deferred with sources; the algebraic time constant itself is in scope.
Exclude AC phasors, reactive power, full network solvers, transients, safety code and hardware installation advice.
starter_sources: https://openstax.org -- navigate to University Physics Volume 2 chapters on Capacitance and Inductance; record exact book, edition and section
special_checks: Divider records must state no-load vs loaded conditions and reject zero-total-resistance inputs
Capacitor and inductor energy records need zero-state references and explicit sign/passivity conventions
